ANSWER: YES

**Quick answer**

`Question as researched`:

The highest tier of GDPR fines is EUR 20 million or 4% of total worldwide annual turnover, whichever is higher. It applies to the most serious infringements listed in Article 83(5).

VERIFIED. Confidence 90%. Four independent sources agree with the regulation text.

## Deep dive

- Article 83(5) sets the higher cap at EUR 20 million or 4% of turnover [1]
- Article 83(4) sets a lower cap of EUR 10 million or 2% [1]
- Sub-question: the cap applies to each infringement decision, and regulators weigh the factors in Article 83(2) [2]
- Guidance from the European Data Protection Board confirms the turnover of the whole undertaking counts [3]
- `Assumptions:`
  1. Turnover means the turnover of the whole group (answer holds if wrong)
- Conflicting evidence:
- What would change this answer: an amendment to Article 83 or a court ruling on the undertaking concept
- Added queries: none

Sources:
[1] European Union. Regulation (EU) 2016/679, General Data Protection Regulation. 2016-05-04. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj Type: primary. Used for: the fine caps in Article 83.
[2] European Data Protection Board. Guidelines on the application and setting of administrative fines. 2023-05-24. https://www.edpb.europa.eu/our-work-tools/our-documents/guidelines_en Type: primary. Used for: how regulators apply the caps.
[3] European Commission. Data protection in the EU. 2024-01-15. https://commission.europa.eu/law/law-topic/data-protection_en Type: secondary. Used for: plain summary of the fine tiers.
[4] GDPR.eu. Fines and penalties. 2023-06-01. https://gdpr.eu/fines/ Type: secondary. Used for: cross-check of the two tiers.
- [5] Information Commissioner's Office. Penalties. 2024-03-01. https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/ Type: secondary. Used for: a national regulator view.
